notes.meaning: The angels gathered again to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came along with them. This second heavenly meeting showed that Satan was actively seeking another opportunity to attack Job. God remains the supreme ruler who holds court over all spiritual beings.

God asked Satan where he had been, and Satan answered that he was roaming all around the earth. Satan was restlessly searching for ways to cause trouble and tempt people to turn from God. Even when evil powers wander about, they must still answer to the Lord.

God pointed out Job again as a blameless and godly man who refused to do evil. He told Satan that Job held tightly to his integrity even though Satan urged God to bring ruin on him without any cause. God showed that true faith can stand firm through terrible losses.

Satan answered with the proverb "skin for skin," claiming a person will give up everything just to save his own life. He argued that Job only accepted the loss of his family and wealth because his own body was still safe. Satan claimed that Job's worship was purely selfish.

Satan asked God to strike Job's actual bones and flesh, claiming this would make Job curse God to His face. He believed that severe physical pain would finally break Job's faith and turn him into a rebel. The devil often uses bodily suffering to tempt believers to turn away from God.

God allowed Satan to afflict Job directly, but gave a strict command to spare Job's life. God placed a boundary around Satan, proving that the enemy can go no further than the Lord permits. Believers can take comfort knowing that God keeps ultimate control over their trials.

Satan left the Lord's presence and struck Job with painful, burning sores from the soles of his feet to the top of his head. This terrible disease left no part of Job's body untouched by agony. God allowed this physical suffering to test and prove the purity of Job's devotion.

Job sat down in the ashes and picked up a piece of broken pottery to scrape his running sores. Sitting among the ashes showed his extreme sorrow and deep humility before God. The rough pottery piece was the only tool he had left to ease his relentless itching and pain.

Job's wife told him to give up his integrity, curse God, and die. Broken by her own grief and her husband's misery, she urged Job to do the exact thing Satan wanted him to do. Even people closest to us can sometimes tempt us to lose hope in God.

Job corrected his wife by saying she spoke like a foolish woman, asking if we should only accept good things from God and never troubles. He remembered that both blessings and trials come under God's sovereign rule. Through all this pain, Job did not say anything sinful against God.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some prosperity teachers claim that Job brought his suffering on himself by speaking fearful or negative words, though commentators note this verse explicitly states Job did not sin in what he said.

notes.meaning: Job's three friends, Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar, heard about all his disasters and traveled from their homes to see him. They agreed to meet together so they could comfort him and share his sorrow. True friends come alongside us when hard times strike.

When the friends saw Job from a distance, they could hardly recognize him because his illness had disfigured him so badly. They cried out loudly, tore their robes, and threw dust into the air over their heads. These traditional customs expressed their overwhelming shock and shared heartbreak.

The three friends sat on the ground with Job for seven days and nights without speaking a single word. They remained quiet because they saw that his pain and grief were far too heavy for ordinary words. Sometimes being present in silence is the best way to care for someone who is hurting.
